# Cairn

> Cairn is a free, open-source (AGPL-3.0) tool that reconciles device
> inventory from your MDM and EDR tools into a single IT asset system of
> record in Snipe-IT, and reports where that record drifts from reality.

Cairn reads device data from the tools that already manage your fleet — Jamf
Pro, Microsoft Intune, Kandji, JumpCloud, Google Workspace (ChromeOS),
CrowdStrike Falcon, Sophos Central, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, Apple
Business Manager, UniFi, CDW, and Rudder, plus lightweight ARP-based network
discovery — matches records for the same physical machine by serial number,
merges them field-by-field by a configurable trust score, and writes one
reconciled record into Snipe-IT (the system of record it writes to; it can
also read drift against GLPI or NetBox). It then pushes the resulting asset
tag back to the source MDM so both sides agree.

Its read-only `cairn drift` command never writes anything: it compares every
connected source against the CMDB and reports devices that are missing,
stale, duplicated, or conflicting, each with a 0–100 confidence score, and can
post a scheduled digest to Slack, Microsoft Teams, or a webhook. `cairn sync
--dry-run` previews every create/update before any write happens.

Cairn is single-binary (macOS, Windows, Linux), free and open source under
the AGPL-3.0 (the same license as Snipe-IT), with no paid tiers, no seat
limits, and no license keys. It's also installable from PyPI as `cairn-sync`.

## Pages

- [Home](https://cairn.dosanjhlabs.com/): product overview, drift report,
  features, integrations, and install instructions.
- [Docs](https://cairn.dosanjhlabs.com/docs.html): setup guide (install,
  connect sources, point at Snipe-IT, dry-run then sync) and FAQ.
- [Pricing](https://cairn.dosanjhlabs.com/pricing.html): free and open
  source, forever — no paid plans, seat limits, or license keys.
- [AI & content-usage policy](https://cairn.dosanjhlabs.com/ai-policy.html):
  how AI/answer crawlers may use this site's content.
